original_title: Adaptive Routing for Meshed QKD Networks of Flexible Size Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
original_authors: Johann, T.; Kühl, S.; Pachnicke, S.
original_method_claim: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Graph Attention Networks (GATs) for hop-wise routing in unknown meshed QKD networks
original_metrics_claim: 18.7% increase in mean key store filling levels vs. shortest-path; zero key store depletion; generalizes to unseen topologies including 14-node NSFNET
original_limitations_claim: Software-based agent; millisecond inference latency; requires offline training; cannot adapt sub-millisecond to key depletion events
original_relevance_claim: PRIMARY COUNTERPART. QFlow targets nanosecond hardware routing vs. this ms-latency DRL agent. Serves as baseline B4.

original_title: Overview of Routing Approaches in Quantum Key Distribution Networks
original_authors: Cvitić, I.; Peraković, D.; Pinto, A.N.
original_method_claim: Systematic survey classifying 26 routing strategies for terrestrial, satellite, and hybrid QKD networks; categories: key-rate-aware, multi-path, RL, SDN
original_metrics_claim: Key-aware dynamic algorithms reduce service rejection 25–40% vs. static SP; multi-path increases resilience but raises key consumption 30–60%
original_limitations_claim: Survey paper only; no hardware implementations; all strategies operate at software/SDN level with ms latency polling
original_relevance_claim: Definitively establishes gap QFlow fills: all 26 reviewed strategies are software-based. QFlow is the first hardware dataplane solution.

original_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Routing and Resource Assignment in QKD-Secured Optical Networks
original_authors: Sharma, P.; Bhatia, V.; Prakash, S.
original_method_claim: DRL-based RRA scheme using DQN; state = QKD lightpath occupancy; outperforms DQN, FF, RF baselines on NSFNET and UBN24 topologies
original_metrics_claim: Lower blocking probability and better resource utilization vs. DQN baseline; demonstrated on 24-node US backbone network
original_limitations_claim: Inference in milliseconds; training data must include quantum channel state; no hardware implementation; not fidelity-decay aware
original_relevance_claim: Baseline B4 design inspiration. QFlow outperforms on latency (ns vs ms) with equal or better path quality.

original_title: A Quantum Key Distribution Routing Scheme for Hybrid-Trusted QKD Network System
original_authors: Chen, L.Q.; Chen, J.Q.; Chen, Q.Y.; Zhao, Y.L.
original_method_claim: Improved Yen's k-shortest-paths + greedy load-balancing; multi-path with both trusted and hybrid-trusted paths; optimizes key consumption
original_metrics_claim: Feasible hybrid-trusted routing; superior load balancing and key consumption vs. single-path; simulation on 6-node network
original_limitations_claim: Greedy heuristic; does not model fidelity decay; software-only; polling-based key pool awareness; not real-time
original_relevance_claim: Related Work: demonstrates multi-objective QKD routing importance. QFlow adds continuous hardware fidelity tracking missing here.

original_title: A Dynamic-Routing Algorithm Based on a Virtual Quantum Key Distribution Network
original_authors: Bi, L.; Miao, M.; Di, X.
original_method_claim: Bayesian link-blocking probability + residual key pool model; combines key quantity and blocking probability for route selection; Mininet simulation
original_metrics_claim: Better congestion avoidance, reduced delay, improved QKD efficiency vs. shortest-path; dynamic QKP sizing reduces resource waste
original_limitations_claim: Software-based; no fidelity model; polling interval introduces staleness; not hardware-accelerated
original_relevance_claim: Demonstrates key-pool-aware routing value. QFlow's SKAG provides real-time updates vs. their periodic polling model.

original_title: Routing Algorithm Within the Multiple Non-Overlapping Paths' Approach for QKD Networks
original_authors: Kiktenko, E.O.; Tayduganov, A.; Fedorov, A.K.
original_method_claim: Multiple non-overlapping paths algorithm to maximize security; path diversity prevents single-point key compromise; analytical throughput model
original_metrics_claim: Maximizes security against node compromise; theoretical throughput analysis; applicable to arbitrary topologies
original_limitations_claim: Ignores key fidelity decay; software routing decision; no real-time key pool state; focus on security not latency
original_relevance_claim: Related Work: multi-path QKD routing context. QFlow extends to fidelity-decay-aware multi-objective optimization in hardware.

original_title: Q-Learning for Resource-Aware and Adaptive Routing in Trusted-Relay QKD Networks
original_method_claim: Q-learning MDP with state = {current node, destination, discretized key occupancy}; reward penalizes imbalance and key depletion
original_metrics_claim: Avg delivery time ~100s vs. 170–590s for baselines; 45.8 vs 118.5 hops average delay; significant utilization improvement under heavy load
original_limitations_claim: Tabular Q-learning; slow convergence; still software; ms-scale decisions; no fidelity-decay model in state space
original_relevance_claim: Recent (2025) RL-routing baseline. Confirms RL routing advantages; QFlow delivers same optimization in nanoseconds via hardware.

original_title: Fast and Secure Routing Algorithms for Quantum Key Distribution Networks
original_method_claim: Tandem Queue Decomposition (TQD) combining UMW routing policy with QKD key generation process; stochastic key availability model
original_metrics_claim: Throughput-optimal policy; achieves entire secure capacity region for unicast/multicast/anycast; polynomial-time algorithm
original_limitations_claim: Theoretical throughput optimality; does not model key fidelity decay; centralized control; not hardware-accelerated
original_relevance_claim: Strong theoretical baseline. QFlow's stochastic SKAG model is motivated by their Poisson key arrival model.

original_title: Dynamic Security-Aware Resource Allocation in QKD-Enabled Optical Networks
original_method_claim: D-SQRA: heuristic that jointly solves routing, wavelength, and time-slot assignment while dynamically adjusting security levels per network load
original_metrics_claim: Lower blocking probability than F-SQRA and B-QRA; adaptive security level reduces unnecessary key consumption under light load
original_limitations_claim: Heuristic; offline optimization; no hardware dataplane; security level adaptation not real-time
original_relevance_claim: Recent QKD resource allocation. QFlow unifies routing + scheduling + key management in hardware at nanosecond scale.

original_title: Routing with Minimum Activated Trusted Nodes in QKD Networks
original_method_claim: ILP formulation minimizing number of activated trusted relay nodes while satisfying key rate and security constraints
original_metrics_claim: Optimal trusted node activation reduces cost 20–35%; applicable to large-scale IoT-integrated QKD networks
original_limitations_claim: ILP solver; exponential worst-case complexity; no fidelity model; software-only; not applicable to real-time routing
original_relevance_claim: Motivates trusted-node-aware routing. QFlow handles this implicitly via SKAG composite weights.

original_title: DRL-based Progressive Recovery for Quantum-Key-Distribution Networks
original_authors: Li, M.; Zhang, Q.; Gatto, A.; Bregni, S.; Verticale, G.; Tornatore, M.
original_venue: Journal of Optical Communications and Networking, 16(4), E36–E47
original_method_claim: DRL for progressive QKD network recovery after failures; trains on simulated QKD network failures; considers key availability during recovery
original_metrics_claim: Faster recovery than static methods; maintains >90% throughput during recovery; evaluated on NSFNET
original_limitations_claim: Recovery scenario only; not for baseline routing; ms latency; no fidelity decay modeling
original_relevance_claim: Extends DRL routing to fault-tolerance. QFlow's SKAG naturally handles link failures (edge weight → infinity).

original_title: Routing, Channel, Key-Rate, and Time-Slot Assignment for QKD in Optical Networks
original_authors: Zhang, Q.; Ayoub, O.; Gatto, A.; Wu, J.; Musumeci, F.; Tornatore, M.
original_venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, 21(1), 148–160
original_method_claim: Joint RCKTA problem formulation as ILP; considers routing, wavelength channel, key-rate, and time-slot simultaneously
original_metrics_claim: Near-optimal joint assignment; significant improvement over separate optimization; validated on COST239 topology
original_limitations_claim: ILP: NP-hard; offline solver; cannot handle real-time key depletion; no fidelity-decay model
original_relevance_claim: Multi-dimensional QKD resource allocation framework. QFlow's SKAG captures similar dimensions but in real-time hardware.

original_title: MadQCI: A Heterogeneous and Scalable SDN-QKD Network Deployed in Production Facilities
original_authors: Martin, V.; Brito, J.P.; Ortíz, L. et al. (EU Consortium)
original_method_claim: SDN-controlled multi-vendor QKD network (28 QKD modules, 9 nodes, 45 links); FPGA-based SoC for signal processing; ETSI QKD 015 standard
original_metrics_claim: Supports 1,230 key requests/s; 0.15ms latency for 5G use case; 500 Mbps encrypted throughput for e-health; production-grade deployment
original_limitations_claim: FPGA used only for physical-layer signal processing (DSP, error correction); routing decisions remain in SDN controller (software); no fidelity-decay aware routing
original_relevance_claim: CRITICAL REFERENCE. Demonstrates real-world SDN-QKD viability. QFlow addresses exactly the SDN controller bottleneck: moves routing to hardware dataplane.

original_title: The Evolution of Quantum Key Distribution Networks: On the Road to the Qinternet
original_authors: Cao, Y.; Zhao, Y.; Wang, Q.; Zhang, J.; Ng, S.X.; Hanzo, L.
original_method_claim: Comprehensive survey of QKD network evolution: key management, routing protocols, SDN integration, trusted-node architectures, future quantum internet
original_metrics_claim: Identifies key management as central challenge; SDN as dominant paradigm; routing latency bottleneck at SDN controller
original_limitations_claim: Survey only; identifies hardware acceleration gap but provides no solution; ms-latency SDN assumed throughout
original_relevance_claim: Foundational reference for QKD network architecture. Confirms SDN controller latency bottleneck that QFlow solves.

original_title: Implementation of Carrier-Grade Quantum Communication Networks over 10,000 km
original_method_claim: China Quantum Communication Network (CN-QCN): 145 fiber backbone nodes, 20 metro networks, 17 provinces; hybrid SDN + trusted relay architecture
original_metrics_claim: World's largest QKD network; 10,000km span; production operation; integrates satellite (Micius) and fiber links
original_limitations_claim: Entire routing infrastructure is software-based SDN; key pool management at software layer; no hardware routing acceleration
original_relevance_claim: Demonstrates scale of QKD deployment where hardware routing acceleration would have transformative impact.

original_title: A Zero-Trust Spatiotemporal Diversification Framework for Multipath QKD
original_method_claim: Dynamic route shuffling for zero-trust security; multipath multi-key distribution; improved Yen's algorithm + greedy selection
original_metrics_claim: Enhanced security against compromised relay attacks; feasibility of zero-trust operation; simulation on 8-node network
original_limitations_claim: Software routing; no fidelity awareness; zero-trust model adds latency overhead; SDN controller dependent
original_relevance_claim: Security-focused QKD routing. QFlow adds hardware speed to comparable security-aware routing decisions.

original_title: Efficient FPGA Implementation of Polar Codes-Based Information Reconciliation for QKD
original_authors: Liao, L.; Wu, X.; Chen, Y. et al. (Sun Yat-sen Univ.)
original_method_claim: Parallel successive-cancellation decoder for polar codes on cost-effective FPGA; pipeline architecture; hardware accelerator for DV-QKD post-processing
original_metrics_claim: Achieves 35 Mbps throughput at 200 MHz; 10–20× improvement over CPU; <1W power consumption; resource utilization <40% on Artix-7
original_limitations_claim: Physical layer only (error correction); no routing capability; no fidelity tracking; cannot make path selection decisions
original_relevance_claim: MOST CITED FPGA-QKD paper. Directly cited in QFlow plan. Shows FPGA for QKD physical layer is mature — QFlow fills the routing layer gap.

original_title: FPGA-Based Implementation of Multidimensional Reconciliation Encoding in QKD
original_authors: Lu, Q.; Lu, Z.; Yang, H.; Yang, S.; Li, Y.
original_method_claim: Circulatory pipeline structure for 8D reconciliation encoding on Xilinx Virtex-7; structural multiplexing; simplified parity-check matrix algorithm
original_metrics_claim: Variable throughput from 0.5–4 Gbps depending on FPGA frequency; 40% lower latency than prior implementations
original_limitations_claim: CV-QKD physical layer only; encoding only; no routing; no key management; specific to Gaussian modulation
original_relevance_claim: FPGA implementation for QKD physical layer. Demonstrates FPGA feasibility for QKD. QFlow targets the higher-layer routing problem.

original_title: Scalable QKD Postprocessing System with Reconfigurable Hardware Accelerator
original_authors: Venkatachalam, N.; Shingala, F.P. et al.
original_method_claim: Reconfigurable FPGA accelerator for QKD post-processing pipeline: sifting, error correction, privacy amplification; AXI-based configuration
original_metrics_claim: Scalable to multiple QKD device rates; 3.5× speedup over CPU; supports BB84, E91 protocols
original_limitations_claim: Post-processing acceleration only; no routing or network-layer decisions; no path selection; no fidelity tracking
original_relevance_claim: IEEE TQE paper. Establishes AXI-based FPGA architecture for QKD (similar to QFlow's AXI-Lite config). Gap: no routing.

original_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to FPGA-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction
original_venue: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Software (QSW)
original_method_claim: Survey and KPI analysis for FPGA-based QEC decoders; identifies mandatory requirements: real-time throughput, latency, power, scalability
original_metrics_claim: Real-time FPGA QEC feasible at sub-microsecond latency; pipeline and parallel architectures dominate; KPIs: <1μs decoding latency requirement
original_limitations_claim: QEC focus only; no QKD routing; survey not implementation; does not address network-layer decisions
original_relevance_claim: Establishes FPGA as the correct platform for quantum-adjacent real-time processing — motivates QFlow's FPGA platform choice.

original_title: FPT-EMS: FPGA Implementation Using NB-LDPC Code for CV-QKD
original_method_claim: HLS-based T-EMS decoder for NB-LDPC codes targeting CV-QKD reconciliation; six pipelined submodules; designed with HLS pragmas
original_metrics_claim: High reconciliation efficiency at low SNR; resource-efficient on Zynq FPGA; competitive throughput vs. GPU implementations
original_limitations_claim: Decoder-only; no network layer; no routing; HLS constraints limit fine-grained optimization
original_relevance_claim: 2025 FPGA-QKD physical layer work. Pattern of FPGA for QKD lower layers is clear; QFlow breaks into network layer.

original_title: FPGA-Based Synchronization of Frequency Domain Interferometer for QKD
original_method_claim: FPGA real-time synchronization of quantum interferometer; sub-nanosecond timing precision; Zynq SoC implementation
original_metrics_claim: Sub-ns sync precision; stable quantum fringe visibility; enables high-rate QKD at > 1 Gbps clock
original_limitations_claim: Physical-layer synchronization only; no routing; no key management; not applicable to network-level decisions
original_relevance_claim: Confirms FPGA sub-nanosecond precision for quantum applications — same principle exploited by QFlow for routing decisions.

original_title: A Fully Customizable Hardware Implementation for General Purpose Genetic Algorithms
original_method_claim: Fully customizable GA IP core for FPGA (VHDL); pipelined + parallel architecture; modular operators (selection, crossover, mutation) as swappable blocks
original_metrics_claim: ~95% reduction in clock cycles per generation vs. previous implementations; finds global optimum on TSP and benchmark functions; 12% LUT utilization
original_limitations_claim: Single-objective GA; general purpose (not quantum-domain-specific); no Pareto front; no domain-specific fitness (no fidelity or key metrics)
original_relevance_claim: CITED IN QFLOW PLAN. The general-purpose GA IP core that QFlow extends with quantum-specific fitness functions, multi-objective Pareto comparators, and SKAG coupling.

original_title: Customizable FPGA IP Core Implementation of a General-Purpose Genetic Algorithm Engine
original_method_claim: GA IP core on Xilinx Virtex-II Pro; parameterizable population/generations/rates; multiple fitness functions supported; BRAM-based chromosome storage
original_metrics_claim: 13% LUT utilization; 50 MHz clock; configurable via register interface; verified on standard benchmarks
original_limitations_claim: Single-objective only; old FPGA technology; no domain-specific operators; no Pareto dominance; 50 MHz limits throughput
original_relevance_claim: Foundational FPGA-GA IP core paper. QFlow's PMO-GA generalizes this to multi-objective with quantum-domain fitness at 200 MHz.

original_title: Automated Framework for General-Purpose Genetic Algorithms in FPGAs
original_authors: Guo, L.; Thomas, D.B.; Luk, W.
original_method_claim: HLS-based automated GA framework; user provides problem specification; generates parameterized FPGA implementation; demonstrated on NP-hard set covering
original_metrics_claim: 30× speedup vs. multi-core CPU; flexible and reusable; demonstrated on 6 benchmark problems including locating and set covering
original_limitations_claim: No multi-objective support; HLS abstraction limits cycle-accurate optimization; no domain-specific quantum operators
original_relevance_claim: Automated FPGA-GA framework. QFlow hand-designs PMO-GA for maximum performance and quantum-domain specificity.

original_title: RapidLayout: Fast Hard Block Placement Using NSGA-II on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs
original_venue: ACM Transactions on Reconfigurable Technology and Systems (TRETS)
original_method_claim: NSGA-II multi-objective evolutionary algorithm for FPGA placement; dual objectives: wirelength² + bounding box; transfer learning between FPGA families
original_metrics_claim: 5–6× faster than Vivado with manual constraints; eliminates weeks of manual placement; Pareto-optimal placements at high frequency
original_limitations_claim: EDA application (placement), not communication routing; runs on CPU not on FPGA itself; different optimization domain
original_relevance_claim: Modern multi-objective NSGA-II with Pareto dominance. QFlow applies similar Pareto mechanisms to quantum routing in hardware.

original_title: A High-Performance, Pipelined, FPGA-Based Genetic Algorithm Machine
original_authors: Shackleford, B.; Snider, G.; Carter, R.
original_venue: Genetic Programming and Evolvable Machines, Springer
original_method_claim: Multi-FPGA pipelined GA; one child per clock cycle by pipelining selection, crossover, mutation, fitness; steady-state memory model
original_metrics_claim: 1 child/clock cycle throughput; solves 94×520 set covering problem; throughput limited only by fitness evaluation depth
original_limitations_claim: Multi-FPGA system required; single-objective; old technology; no BRAM-based memory hierarchy
original_relevance_claim: Seminal paper on pipelined FPGA-GA. QFlow's 5-stage PMO-GA pipeline is inspired by this one-child-per-cycle approach.

original_title: Hardware Implementation of Genetic Algorithm on FPGA
original_venue: IEEE Midwest Symposium on Circuits and Systems (MWSCAS)
original_method_claim: Parallel-pipelined hardware GA (PPHGA) in VHDL; handshaking protocol between modules; verified on 3 applications (interpolation, thermistor, vehicle)
original_metrics_claim: Autonomous parallel operation; correctness verified on engineering applications; modular VHDL design
original_limitations_claim: Early implementation; limited parameterization; no multi-objective; resource usage not optimized
original_relevance_claim: Historical FPGA-GA implementation. Demonstrates modular VHDL decomposition approach adopted by QFlow's module separation.

original_title: RELiQ: Scalable Entanglement Routing via Reinforcement Learning in Quantum Networks
original_authors: Meuser, T. et al. (TU Darmstadt group)
original_method_claim: RL-based entanglement routing using GNN with local information only; iterative message exchange between repeaters; trained on random graphs
original_metrics_claim: Outperforms global-information heuristics; constant per-node load regardless of network size; scales to 1000 repeaters
original_limitations_claim: Software RL agent; inference latency in ms; no hardware implementation; fidelity modeled but tracking not in hardware
original_relevance_claim: CITED IN QFLOW PLAN. State-of-the-art software routing. QFlow provides hardware equivalent — same fidelity awareness, 1000× faster decisions.

original_title: qRL: Reinforcement Learning Routing for Quantum Entanglement Networks
original_method_claim: Quantum-aware RL routing protocol; two-stage: (1) efficient route finding, (2) entanglement swapping and purification scheduling
original_metrics_claim: Superior end-to-end route fidelity; significantly higher request success rates vs. traditional methods across multiple network sizes
original_limitations_claim: Software agent; training required per topology; ms latency; entanglement-focused (not key-pool-focused for QKD)
original_relevance_claim: Fidelity-aware RL routing. QFlow tracks fidelity in dedicated FDPE hardware and routes without RL inference delays.

original_title: QoS-Aware Reinforcement Learning Routing for Entanglement Networks
original_method_claim: RL with fidelity-aware rewards; utility-based scheduling; models decoherence and quantum memory constraints; compares to DQRA and Proactive baselines
original_metrics_claim: 0.05–0.10 fidelity advantage over DQRA; 0.15–0.20 over Proactive; better queue management under bursty traffic
original_limitations_claim: Preprint; software only; high classical coordination overhead; decoherence modeled but no hardware prediction
original_relevance_claim: Latest QoS-fidelity routing. QFlow's FDPE performs continuous hardware decoherence prediction — what this paper does in software.

original_title: Entanglement Routing for Quantum Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
original_method_claim: DRL-based entanglement routing; state includes fidelity and memory capacity; reward based on fidelity and delivery rate
original_metrics_claim: Significant improvements in routing fidelity and delivery rates vs. Dijkstra-based methods; demonstrated on 20-node networks
original_limitations_claim: Software DRL; training required; fidelity-aware but not key-pool-aware; no hardware implementation
original_relevance_claim: Early fidelity-aware DRL routing paper. Establishes that fidelity must be a first-class routing metric — core QFlow premise.

original_title: Robust Belief-State Policy Learning for Quantum Network Routing Under Decoherence
original_method_claim: POMDP + GNN hybrid for quantum routing; belief-state compression for partial observability; noise-adaptive mechanism for decoherence
original_metrics_claim: Fidelity 0.917 ± 0.034; 1.4× higher delivery under peak demand; scales to 300-node networks; 67% qubit utilization
original_limitations_claim: Preprint; computationally expensive POMDP belief update; software only; seconds-scale training requirement
original_relevance_claim: Most mathematically sophisticated software routing. QFlow achieves comparable fidelity-awareness in nanoseconds without belief inference.

original_title: Optimal Key Forwarding Strategy in QKD Behaviours
original_method_claim: LP formulation for key forwarding and redistribution at KMS level; three scenarios: all-to-all, one-to-all, one-to-one; maximization of key redistribution
original_metrics_claim: Optimal redistribution computed via LP; performance depends heavily on network size and graph topology
original_limitations_claim: LP solver (offline); no real-time key tracking; no fidelity model; KMS-level only; cannot react to decoherence events
original_relevance_claim: Key forwarding optimization at KMS level. QFlow provides real-time hardware equivalent of their LP solution.

original_title: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) for Industrial Automation: Current Advances and Future Directions
original_method_claim: Comprehensive survey of TSN standards: IEEE 802.1Qbv (TAS), 802.1Qbu (preemption), 802.1AS (sync), 802.1CB (redundancy); applications and open challenges
original_metrics_claim: 802.1Qbv achieves bounded e2e latency with GCL; NP-hard scheduling problem; RL emerging for dynamic reconfiguration
original_limitations_claim: Industrial automation context; no quantum application; scheduling NP-hard; GCL reconfiguration at centralized level
original_relevance_claim: QFlow adopts 802.1Qbv for QP-TSN scheduler. This survey establishes the TSN mechanism QFlow adapts for quantum priority traffic.

original_title: Real-Time Scheduling for 802.1Qbv Time-Sensitive Networking: A Systematic Review and Experimental Study
original_method_claim: Systematic review of 17 TSN scheduling methods: FR, NW, SMT models; experimental comparison on hardware testbed; GCL configuration study
original_metrics_claim: No-wait model minimizes latency; SMT-NW optimal for small networks; ML-based scheduling gaining traction; hardware GCL latency measured
original_limitations_claim: Industrial focus; no quantum; GCL reconfiguration latency at ms scale in centralized models
original_relevance_claim: Validates that GCL-based TSN achieves bounded latency. QFlow's QP-TSN implements microsecond hardware GCL swap vs their ms centralized approach.

original_title: Configuring the IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Aware Shaper with Deep Reinforcement Learning
original_method_claim: DRL for online 802.1Qbv configuration in reconfigurable production networks; learns GCL configuration without prior flow knowledge
original_metrics_claim: Handles open networks where flows change; avoids expensive ILP solver; reduces scheduling time in reconfigurable networks
original_limitations_claim: DRL configuration still has ms inference latency; industrial focus; no quantum priority class
original_relevance_claim: DRL-based TSN configuration. QFlow uses hardware FSM for deterministic GCL reconfiguration triggered by GA output.

original_title: P4-Based Programmable Data Plane for In-Network Computing
original_method_claim: P4 language for programmable packet processing; match-action pipeline in network hardware; enables in-network ML inference
original_metrics_claim: Nanosecond-scale packet processing in ASIC/FPGA; enables routing decisions without CPU intervention; adopted by major switch vendors
original_limitations_claim: Fixed match-action pipeline; limited compute; no BRAM-based graph state; cannot run iterative optimization
original_relevance_claim: Demonstrates nanosecond data-plane routing decisions. QFlow extends this concept with a graph-state-aware routing engine specific to QKD.

original_title: Reconfigurable Network Processing at Line Rate: Challenges and Approaches
original_method_claim: Survey of FPGA/ASIC network processor architectures for line-rate processing; pipeline depth analysis; resource-throughput trade-off
original_metrics_claim: Line-rate processing requires deep pipelining; BRAM-based state enables nanosecond graph lookups; FPGA achieves 100+ Gbps routing
original_limitations_claim: Classical networks focus; no quantum-specific considerations; no graph-based optimization
original_relevance_claim: Architecture foundation for QFlow. Confirms FPGA pipeline + BRAM is the right approach for nanosecond network processing.

original_title: Piecewise-Linear Approximation of Mathematical Functions in FPGA: Survey and Design Methodology
original_method_claim: Survey and methodology for LUT-based piecewise-linear approximation of transcendental functions (exp, log, trig) in FPGA using fixed-point arithmetic
original_metrics_claim: Error < 0.1% achievable with 256-entry LUT; Q0.16 fixed-point sufficient for most signal processing; DSP slices minimize resource usage
original_limitations_claim: Accuracy/resource trade-off must be characterized per application; overflow handling required
original_relevance_claim: Direct methodology for QFlow's FDPE exponential decay LUT (256-entry, Q0.16, <0.1% error as specified in the architecture plan).

original_title: Hardware-Efficient Random Number Generation for FPGAs: Xorshift and LFSR Comparison
original_authors: Marsaglia, G. et al. (and follow-up hardware implementations)
original_method_claim: Xorshift128+ PRNG implementation on FPGA; period 2^128-1; hardware-friendly XOR+shift operations; statistical quality vs LFSR comparison
original_metrics_claim: Xorshift128+ passes all NIST statistical tests; 1 random number per clock at 200 MHz; 3× better statistical quality than LFSR of same size
original_limitations_claim: Cryptographically not secure; period finite; multiple instances need different seeds
original_relevance_claim: Directly used in QFlow PMO-GA random path generation. Justifies Xorshift128+ choice over LFSR as stated in the plan.

original_title: A Survey of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) Network Simulation Platforms
original_venue: IEEE International Conference on High Performance Switching and Routing (HPSR)
original_method_claim: Survey of simulation tools for QKD networks: NS-3 QKD module, OMNeT++ QKD, SimQN, NetSquid; comparison of capabilities
original_metrics_claim: OMNeT++ most flexible for protocol development; NS-3 integrates with classical network simulation; SimQN fastest for large-scale
original_limitations_claim: Survey only; no performance comparison; simulation fidelity varies across platforms
original_relevance_claim: Justifies OMNeT++ choice for Phase 4 simulation in QFlow plan. Survey confirms OMNeT++ is standard for QKD network research.

original_title: NetSquid: A Network Simulator for Quantum Information using Discrete Events
original_method_claim: Discrete-event quantum network simulator; models entanglement generation, decoherence, quantum memory, measurement; Python-based
original_metrics_claim: Sub-second simulation of 25-node networks; validated against analytical models; models T1/T2 decoherence times
original_limitations_claim: Entanglement-focused (not QKD key distribution specifically); Python overhead limits large-scale simulations
original_relevance_claim: Decoherence model (T1/T2 times) directly informs QFlow's FDPE exponential decay model. Key parameter T2 for coherence time.

original_title: Information Reconciliation of CV-QKD: Principles, Implementations and Applications
original_method_claim: Survey of reconciliation schemes: slice, multidimensional, LDPC/polar codes; hardware acceleration on FPGA and GPU; rate-compatible codes
original_metrics_claim: FPGA achieves 10–100× speedup over CPU for IR; LDPC codes dominate; hardware rate-compatible codes enable adaptive systems
original_limitations_claim: Physical layer only; no routing; no key management after IR; no network-layer awareness
original_relevance_claim: Establishes FPGA for QKD physical layer. QFlow is positioned as the natural next layer above IR in FPGA-accelerated QKD stack.

original_title: Quantum Key Distribution: A Networking Perspective
original_method_claim: Survey of QKD networking: protocols, key management systems, routing, SDN integration, security analysis; 10+ year literature review
original_metrics_claim: Key management identified as central networking challenge; routing bottleneck at SDN controller; fidelity/QBER as key routing metrics
original_limitations_claim: 2020 survey; misses 2023–2025 advances; no hardware dataplane routing considered; SDN assumed as routing paradigm
original_relevance_claim: Foundational networking survey for QKD. Explicitly identifies the software routing bottleneck that QFlow addresses.

original_title: NSGA-II: A Fast and Elitist Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm
original_authors: Deb, K.; Pratap, A.; Agarwal, S.; Meyarivan, T.
original_method_claim: Non-dominated Sorting GA II (NSGA-II); fast non-dominated sort O(MN²); crowding distance; elitism; Pareto-front convergence
original_metrics_claim: Converges to true Pareto front; better diversity than NSGA-I; outperforms PAES and SPEA on benchmark MOPs
original_limitations_claim: Computationally expensive sorting; CPU-based; quadratic complexity in population size; not hardware-pipelined
original_relevance_claim: Foundation for QFlow's PMO-GA Pareto dominance comparators. Hardware parallel comparators replace NSGA-II's sequential sort.

original_title: MOEA/D: A Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition
original_method_claim: Tchebycheff decomposition converts MOP into scalar subproblems; neighborhood-based selection; competitive with NSGA-II on DTLZ benchmarks
original_metrics_claim: Competitive with NSGA-II; better hypervolume on some benchmarks; Tchebycheff decomposition enables tunable objective weighting
